title: Rohinton Mistry emigrates to Canada
text: Rohinton Mistry is an Indian-born Canadian writer. He has been the recipient of the Neustadt International Prize for Literature in 2012.

title: First Canadian Place opens in Toronto
text: First Canadian Place is a commercial skyscraper in the Financial District of Toronto, Ontario, at the northwest corner of King and Bay streets, and serves as the global operational executive office of the Bank of Montreal. At 298 metres tall, it is the third-tallest building in Canada, the 35th-tallest building in North America, and the 261st-tallest in the world.

title: Colin Thatcher, who would later become famous for his involvement in the murder of his ex-wife, is elected to the Saskatchewan Legislative Assembly.
text: Wilbert Colin Thatcher is a Canadian politician who was convicted for the murder of his ex-wife, JoAnn Wilson.

title: In June, 1975 Ovivo, a water and wastewater treatment and purification company, is founded in Quebec as Laperrière & Verreault Inc. (rebranded in 2010).
text: Ovivo is a water and wastewater treatment and purification company. The company is owned by SKion Water GmbH, a subsidiary of German entrepreneur Susanne Klatten’s investment holding SKion GmbH. Ovivo's Head Office is located in Montreal, in the province of Quebec.

title: “Third Rate Romance” by The Amazing Rhythm Aces
text: "Third Rate Romance" is a song written by Russell Smith, first recorded in Montreal in 1974 by Jesse Winchester and his band the Rhythm Aces, assisted by Smith. It became a hit the following year by the newly re-formed Amazing Rhythm Aces on its 1975 album Stacked Deck.
listen: Third Rate Romance The Amazing Rhythm Aces

title: “I'm Sorry” by John Denver
text: "I'm Sorry" is a song written and recorded by American country-folk singer-songwriter John Denver and released in 1975. It was the final number-one pop hit released during his career.

title: “Black Superman (Muhammad Ali)” by Johnny Wakelin
text: "Black Superman" is a song by English songwriter Johnny Wakelin from his album of the same name. The song reached #7 on the UK Singles Chart and #21 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1975.

title: “That's the Way (I Like It)” by KC and the Sunshine Band
text: "That's the Way" is a song by American disco and funk band KC and the Sunshine Band from their self-titled second studio album (1975). The single became the band's second No.
listen: That's the Way (I Like It) KC and the Sunshine Band

title: “Wasted Days and Wasted Nights” by Freddy Fender
text: "Wasted Days and Wasted Nights" is an American country and pop song recorded by Freddy Fender. It is considered by many to belong to the swamp pop idiom of south Louisiana and southeast Texas that had such a major musical impact on Fender.
listen: Wasted Days and Wasted Nights Freddy Fender

title: “Angie Baby” by Helen Reddy
text: "Angie Baby" is a song written by American singer-songwriter Alan O'Day which became a hit for Australian singer Helen Reddy. The song reached #1 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart December 28, 1974, and became one of Reddy's biggest-selling singles.

title: “Fight the Power” by The Isley Brothers
text: "Fight the Power"") is a song recorded by the Isley Brothers; the band released the song as the first single off their landmark album, The Heat Is On. The song is notable for the usage of the word "bullshit", which was censored during radio airplay.
listen: Fight the Power The Isley Brothers

title: “Jackie Blue” by Ozark Mountain Daredevils
text: "Jackie Blue" is a track recorded by the Ozark Mountain Daredevils for their second album It'll Shine When It Shines released in 1974. It was written by band members Larry Lee and Steve Cash with lead vocals by Lee.

title: “Fire” by Ohio Players
text: "Fire" is a song by R&B/funk band Ohio Players. It was the opening track from the album of the same name and hit No.

title: “Magic” by Pilot
text: "Magic" is a 1974 song by Scottish pop rock band Pilot and was the first hit single for the group. It was written by band members David Paton and Billy Lyall for their debut album From the Album of the Same Name.

title: “Please Mr. Postman” by The Carpenters
text: "Please Mr. Postman" is a song written by Georgia Dobbins, William Garrett, Freddie Gorman, Brian Holland and Robert Bateman.

title: “Sister Golden Hair” by America
text: "Sister Golden Hair" is a song by the band America from their fifth album Hearts, written by Gerry Beckley. It was their second single to reach number one on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100, remaining in the top position for one week.

title: “Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds” by Elton John
text: "Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles from their 1967 album Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band.
wiki: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds
listen: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds Elton John

title: “Mandy” by Barry Manilow
text: "Brandy", later called "Mandy", is a song written by Scott English and Richard Kerr. It was originally recorded by English in 1971 and reached the top 20 of the UK Singles Chart.

title: “Have You Never Been Mellow” by Olivia Newton-John
text: "Have You Never Been Mellow" is a song recorded by British-Australian singer Olivia Newton-John for her 1975 fifth studio album of the same name. Written and produced by John Farrar, the song was released as the lead single from the album in January 1975.
listen: Have You Never Been Mellow Olivia Newton-John

title: “Could It Be Magic” by Barry Manilow
text: "Could It Be Magic" is a song written by Adrienne Anderson and composed by American singer-songwriter Barry Manilow, inspired by Frédéric Chopin's Prelude in C minor, Opus 28, Number 20. The song was initially released in 1971 by Featherbed, produced and co-written by Tony Orlando.
listen: Could It Be Magic Barry Manilow

title: “Cat's in the Cradle” by Harry Chapin
text: "Cat's in the Cradle" is a folk rock song by American singer-songwriter Harry Chapin, from his fourth studio album, Verities & Balderdash. The single topped the US Billboard Hot 100 in December 1974.
listen: Cat's in the Cradle Harry Chapin

title: “Wildfire” by Michael Martin Murphey
text: "Wildfire" is a song written by Michael Murphey and Larry Cansler. It was originally recorded by Murphey, who had yet to add his middle name to his recorded work, and appears on his gold-plus 1975 album Blue Sky – Night Thunder.

title: “I'm Not Lisa” by Jessi Colter
text: "I'm Not Lisa" is the most successful song by American country music artist Jessi Colter. It was released on January 16, 1975, as the lead single from her album I'm Jessi Colter.

title: “Listen to What the Man Said” by Wings
text: "Listen to What the Man Said" is a hit single from Wings' 1975 album Venus and Mars. The song featured new member Joe English on drums, with guest musicians Dave Mason on guitar and Tom Scott on soprano saxophone.
wiki: Listen to What the Man Said
listen: Listen to What the Man Said Wings

title: “I'm Not in Love” by 10cc
text: "I'm Not in Love" is a song by the English band 10cc, written by band members Eric Stewart and Graham Gouldman. It is known for its innovative and distinctive backing track, composed mostly of multitracked vocals.

title: “I Can Help” by Billy Swan
text: "I Can Help" is a song written and performed by Billy Swan. Released in July 1974, it became a big crossover smash some four months later, reaching No.

title: “Fallin' in Love” by Hamilton, Joe Frank & Reynolds
text: "Fallin' In Love" is a song by American music trio Hamilton, Joe Frank & Reynolds. It was written by band member Dan Hamilton and featured on the trio's third studio album by the same name.
wiki: Fallin' in Love (Hamilton, Joe Frank & Reynolds song)
listen: Fallin' in Love Hamilton, Joe Frank & Reynolds

title: “Feelings” by Morris Albert
text: "Feelings" is a song written and performed by the Brazilian singer Morris Albert. It was released in June 1974 on Albert's debut album After We've Left Each Other.

title: “When Will I Be Loved” by Linda Ronstadt
text: "When Will I Be Loved" is a popular song written by Phil Everly of the Everly Brothers, who had a US top-ten hit with it in 1960. Linda Ronstadt covered the song in 1975, and her version was an even bigger hit in the US, peaking at No.
listen: When Will I Be Loved Linda Ronstadt

title: “Chevy Van” by Sammy Johns
text: "Chevy Van" is a song by American singer and songwriter Sammy Johns, written and sung by Johns. The song was originally released in 1973 by GRC Records on Johns' debut album, which was also released in 1973.

title: “You're the First, the Last, My Everything” by Barry White
text: "You're the First, the Last, My Everything" is a song recorded by the American singer and songwriter Barry White from his third album, Can't Get Enough. The song was written by White, Tony Sepe and Peter Radcliffe and produced by White.
wiki: You're the First, the Last, My Everything
listen: You're the First, the Last, My Everything Barry White

title: “Please Mr. Please” by Olivia Newton-John
text: "Please Mr. Please" is a song written by Bruce Welch and John Rostill, both members of British pop singer Cliff Richard's backing band, The Shadows.

title: “You're No Good” by Linda Ronstadt
text: "You're No Good" is a song written by Clint Ballard Jr., first performed by Dee Dee Warwick for Jubilee Records in 1963 with production by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller. It has since been covered by many artists, including charting versions by Betty Everett in 1963, the Swinging Blue Jeans in 1964, and Linda Ronstadt in 1974, whose version was a number 1 hit in the United States.

title: “Dynomite” by Bazuka
text: "Dynomite" is a song written by Tony Camillo and performed by Bazuka. The song was featured on their 1975 album, Bazuka.

title: “Walking in Rhythm” by The Blackbyrds
text: "Walking in Rhythm" is a song by American group the Blackbyrds. It tells the tale of a man who is passionate about getting back home to his female companion.

title: “The Way We Were/Try to Remember” by Gladys Knight & the Pips
text: "The Way We Were" is a song by American singer Barbra Streisand from her fifteenth studio album of the same name. It was released as the album's lead single on September 27, 1973, on Columbia Records.
listen: The Way We Were/Try to Remember Gladys Knight & the Pips

title: “Midnight Blue” by Melissa Manchester
text: "Midnight Blue" is a song by American singer and songwriter Melissa Manchester, written by herself alongside Carole Bayer Sager and produced by Vini Poncia with an executive production by Richard Perry. It was released in April 1975 as the first single from Manchester's third studio album, Melissa.

title: “Don't Call Us, We'll Call You” by Sugarloaf
text: "Don't Call Us, We'll Call You" is a hit song by the American rock band Sugarloaf. Co-written by lead vocalist Jerry Corbetta, the song was featured as the title track of the band's fourth and final album.
wiki: Don't Call Us, We'll Call You
listen: Don't Call Us, We'll Call You Sugarloaf

title: Vietnam War: North Vietnamese troops attack Ban Mê Thuột in South Vietnam on their way to capturing Saigon.
text: Buôn Ma Thuột is a ward and the administrative center of Đắk Lắk province, Vietnam. The ward inherited its name from the former city of Buôn Ma Thuột, which was the provincial capital of Đắk Lắk.

title: An extended portion of Sanyō Shinkansen between Okayama Station and Hakata Station opens, giving the Japanese Shinkansen high speed rail network access to the country's second island, Kyushu.
text: The San'yō Shinkansen is a line of the Japanese Shinkansen high-speed rail network, connecting Shin-Osaka in Osaka with Hakata Station in Fukuoka, the two largest cities in western Japan. Operated by the West Japan Railway Company (JR West), it is a westward continuation of the Tōkaidō Shinkansen and also serves other major cities in between on Honshu and Kyushu islands such as Kobe, Himeji, Okayama, Hiroshima, an…

title: The leftist military government in Portugal defeats a rightist coup attempt involving former president António de Spínola, who flees to Brazil.
text: António Sebastião Ribeiro de Spínola was a Portuguese military officer, author and conservative politician. During the Estado Novo regime he became one of Portugal's most senior military commanders, leading military operations against independence movements.

title: Vietnam War: South Vietnam President Nguyễn Văn Thiệu orders the Central Highlands evacuated. This turns into a mass exodus involving troops and civilians (the "Convoy of Tears").
text: Nguyễn Văn Thiệu was a South Vietnamese military officer and politician who was the president of South Vietnam from 1967 to 1975. He was a general in the Republic of Vietnam Armed Forces (RVNAF), became head of a military junta in 1965, and then president after winning a rigged election in 1967.

title: "Ding-a-dong" by Teach-In (music by Dick Bakker, lyrics by Will Luikinga and Eddy Ouwens) wins the 20th Eurovision Song Contest 1975 (staged in Stockholm) for the Netherlands.
text: Teach-In was a Dutch band active from 1967 until 1980. After scoring several top 20 hits in their home country by the early 1970s, the band came to international attention by winning the Eurovision Song Contest 1975 with the song "Ding-a-dong”.

title: King Faisal of Saudi Arabia is shot and killed by his nephew.
text: Faisal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was King of Saudi Arabia from 1964 until his assassination in 1975. Before his ascension, he served as Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia from 1953 to 1964, and he was briefly regent to his half-brother King Saud in 1964.

title: The South African government announces that it will consolidate the 113 separate homeland areas into 36.
text: A homeland is a place where a national or ethnic identity has formed. The definition can also mean simply one's country of birth.

title: A fire in the maternity wing at Kučić Hospital in Rijeka, Yugoslavia (Croatia), kills 25 people.
text: The Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, known from 1945 to 1963 as the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia, and commonly referred to as Yugoslavia, was a country in Central and Southeast Europe. It was established in 1945, following World War II, and lasted until 1992, dissolving amid the onset of the Yugoslav Wars.

title: Süleyman Demirel of AP forms the new government of Turkey (39th government), a four-party coalition, the so-called First National Front (Turkish: Milliyetçi cephe ).
text: Süleyman Sami Demirel was a Turkish politician, engineer, and statesman who served as the president of Turkey from 1993 to 2000. He previously served as the prime minister of Turkey seven times between 1965 and 1993.

title: Vietnam War: The first military Operation Babylift flight, C5A 80218, crashes 27 minutes after takeoff, killing 138 on board; 176 survive the crash.
text: Operation Babylift was a mass evacuation of children from South Vietnam to the United States and other Western countries at the end of the Vietnam War, in April 1975. Over 3,300 infants and children were airlifted, although the actual number has been variously reported.

title: Bill Gates and Paul Allen found Microsoft (at this time known as Micro-Soft) in Albuquerque, New Mexico and release their Altair BASIC interpreter. (Microsoft becomes a registered trademark on November 26, 1976.)April 4: Allen and Gates…
text: William Henry Gates III is an American businessman and philanthropist. A pioneer of the microcomputer revolution of the 1970s and 1980s, he co-founded the software company Microsoft in 1975 with his childhood friend Paul Allen.

title: The Soviet crewed space mission (Soyuz 18a) ends in failure during its ascent into orbit when a critical malfunction occurs in the second and third stages of the booster rocket during staging at an altitude of 192 km, resulting in the…
text: In celestial mechanics, an orbit is the curved trajectory of an object under the influence of an attracting force. Alternatively, it is known as an orbital revolution, because it is a rotation around an axis external to the moving body.

title: Eight people in South Korea, who are involved in the People's Revolutionary Party Incident, are hanged.April 9–21: Battle of Xuân Lộc
text: The Battle of Xuân Lộc was the last major battle of the Vietnam War that took place at Xuân Lộc, Biên Hòa Province (today Đồng Nai Province). Over a period of 12 days between 9 and 21 April 1975, the outnumbered South Vietnamese attempted to stop the North Vietnamese forces from overrunning the town and breaking through towards South Vietnam's capital, Saigon.

title: Bus massacre: The Kataeb militia kills 27 Palestinians during an attack on their bus in Ain El Remmeneh, Lebanon, triggering the Lebanese Civil War which lasts until 1990.
text: The 1975 Beirut bus massacre, also known as the Ain el-Rammaneh incident and Black Sunday, was the collective name given to a short series of armed clashes involving Phalangist and Palestinian elements in the streets of central Beirut, which is commonly presented as the spark that set off the Lebanese Civil War in the mid-1970s.

title: A coup d'état in Chad led by the military overthrows and kills President François Tombalbaye.
text: François Tombalbaye, also known as N'Garta Tombalbaye, was a Chadian politician who served as the first President of Chad from the country's independence in 1960 until his overthrow in 1975. A dictatorial leader, his divisive policies as president led to factional conflict and a pattern of authoritarian leadership and political instability that is still relevant in Chad today.

title: The Khmer Republic surrenders, when the Communist Khmer Rouge guerilla forces capture Phnom Penh ending the Cambodian Civil War, with mass evacuation of American troops and Cambodian civilians.
text: The Cambodian Civil War was a civil war in Cambodia fought by the Khmer Rouge against the government of the Kingdom of Cambodia. Following the March 1970 coup, the conflict shifted as the Khmer Rouge and forces loyal to Norodom Sihanouk, now supported by North Vietnam and China, fought against the Khmer Republic, which was supported by the United States and South Vietnam.

title: The Khmer Rouge begins a forcible mass evacuation of the city and starts the Cambodian genocide.
text: An emergency evacuation is an immediate egress or escape of people away from an area that contains an imminent threat, an ongoing threat or a hazard to lives or property. Examples range from the small-scale evacuation of a building due to a storm or fire to the large-scale evacuation of a city because of a flood, bombardment or approaching weather system, especially a tropical cyclone.

title: Nico Diederichs becomes the 3rd State President of South Africa.
text: Nicolaas Johannes Diederichs, served as the third state president of South Africa from 1975 to 1978.

title: Taman Mini Indonesia Indah opens to the public in Jakarta, Indonesia.
text: Taman Mini Indonesia Indah is a culture-based recreational area located in East Jakarta, Indonesia. Since July 2021, it is operated by Injourney Destination Management (PT Taman Wisata Candi Borobudur, Prambanan, dan Ratu Boko), a subsidiary of the state-owned tourism holding company InJourney.

title: West German Embassy siege in Stockholm: Six Red Army Faction terrorists take over the West German embassy in Stockholm, take 11 hostages and demand the release of the group's jailed members; shortly after, they are captured by Swedish…
text: The West German Embassy siege in Stockholm, Sweden, was a hostage standoff initiated by the Red Army Faction on 24 April 1975. Collectively, the attackers referred to themselves as Kommando Holger Meins, after Holger Meins, an RAF member who had died of starvation during a (collective) hunger strike in Wittlich Prison on 9 November 1974.
wiki: West German Embassy siege in Stockholm

title: Vietnam War: As North Vietnamese Army forces close in on the South Vietnamese capital Saigon, the Australian Embassy is closed and evacuated, almost 10 years to the day since the first Australian troop commitment to South Vietnam.
text: The People's Army of Vietnam is the national military force of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam and the armed wing of the ruling Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV). PAVN is the core component of the Vietnam People's Armed Forces and includes: Ground Force, Navy, Air Defence - Air Force, Border Guard and Coast Guard.

title: Vietnam War: North Vietnam concludes its East Sea Campaign by capturing all of the Spratly Islands that were being held by South Vietnam.
text: The East Sea and Spratly Islands Campaign was a naval operation which took place during the closing days of the Vietnam War in April 1975. The operation took place on Spratly Islands and other islands in the South China Sea (known in Vietnam as the East Sea).
